subject: maths
topic: Coordinate geometry: gradient, distance, midpoint, equation of a line

kept.q: Calculate the gradient of the straight line passing through the points A(-3, 5) and B(1, -3).
kept.explanation: Gradient = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) = (-3 - 5)/(1 - (-3)) = -8/4 = -2. So the gradient of the line is -2.
kept.pidgin: Gradient na (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) = (-3 - 5)/(1 - (-3)) = -8/4 = -2. So the answer na -2.

kept.q: Find the distance between the points P(-4, 1) and Q(2, 9) on the Cartesian plane.
kept.pidgin: Distance = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(36+64) = sqrt(100) = 10. So PQ na 10 units.

kept.q: The midpoint of the line segment joining A(2, -5) and B(x, y) is M(4, 1). Find the value of x + y.
kept.explanation: Using midpoint formula, 4 = (2+x)/2, so x = 6. Also 1 = (-5+y)/2, so y = 7. Therefore x + y = 6 + 7 = 13.
kept.pidgin: From midpoint formula, 4 = (2+x)/2, so x = 6. Also 1 = (-5+y)/2, so y = 7. So x + y = 6+7 = 13.

kept.q: Find the value of m for which the line y = mx + 3 is parallel to the line passing through the points (1, 2) and (4, 11).
kept.explanation: First find the gradient of the line through (1,2) and (4,11): m = (11-2)/(4-1) = 9/3 = 3. Since parallel lines have equal gradients, m must also equal 3.
